key_insight: An analytical model predicts how laser-driven phase change and two-phase choking generate transient microfluidic suction and wall shear capable of removing surface contaminants.
engineering_relevance: The equations offer design rules for coaxial microfluidic actuators, including an inlet-temperature limit intended to sustain continuous suction cycles.
method: Model laser-driven vapor cavity growth and cavitation collapse.
Couple vapor dynamics, nonlinear flow restriction, and drag in closed-form equations.
Represent the curved capillary interface using a two-radii Young–Laplace relation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports predicted pressure drops of 0.25 atm, fluid velocities of 2.50 m/s, and maximum wall shear stress of 30.06 Pa, but describes no experimental validation.
watch_item: The claimed contaminant-removal and substrate-safety thresholds need validation for specific materials and operating conditions.
paper_title: An Analytical Model for Laser-Activated Two-Phase Choking and Microfluidic Suction on Surface Boundary Layers
